description: We are a team of college students tackling Abandoned but not forgotten challenge,  we are trying to build a helpful and friendly platform which can help people of all background to learn about nasa . We developed an interactive game to let players know about human discarded equipment on Moon and Mars. " Join us to make a lasting impact!
summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is a free, kid-friendly website that tells the story of the equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars, such as the Apollo lunar rovers and landers and the Mars rovers Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and InSight.
The site explains where each machine is, how long it worked compared to its plan, and why it was left behind. For example, Opportunity worked for about 14 years after a 90-day mission.
To make learning fun, we built four games: Dust Dash, Mission Quiz, Sort the Gear, and Rocket Quest, a space adventure through Mars, a black hole and a boss fight. We also wrote an original sing-along song, "Stars Are Calling", about exploring space.
The project shows that old space hardware still has stories to teach. It helps children see that nothing in space is truly forgotten. It runs in any browser, with no installation
details:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is a free, kid-friendly website that tells the story of the equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars, including the Apollo lunar rovers and landers and the Mars rovers Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and InSight. Each machine has a card showing where it is, when it last worked, and a "did you know" fact. A bar chart compares how long the rovers were planned to work with how long they actually lasted.
Four games make the history fun for children. In Dust Dash, a rover collects samples and learns facts. Mission Quiz tests what children have learned. Sort the Gear sorts equipment by where it was left. Rocket Quest is a story adventure from Earth to Mars, through a black hole and a white hole, to a boss fight. The site also has an original sing-along song, "Stars Are Calling", with lyrics.
The benefit is that children learn space history by playing, and see that old machines still have stories. The site runs in any browser, with no install, and works on phones and computers.
It is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, the Canvas 2D API for the games, and the Web Audio API. The song was made with Python code (NumPy and SciPy) and FFmpeg. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. Our team considered ease of use for young children, safe content with no ads or accounts, accuracy, and fun.
